findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects (including the customer master data uploaded to it) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption.

No ACL or public access block is configured and the resource is explicitly commented as public; without aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or a private ACL the bucket and its sensitive customer-master.xlsx object can be exposed to anonymous readers.
No logging block is defined, so read/write access to a bucket holding customer master data is not recorded, hampering detection and forensic investigation of unauthorised access.

Versioning is not enabled, so objects can be overwritten or deleted irrecoverably by an attacker (or ransomware) with write access, and force_destroy = true further allows the bucket and all contents to be deleted without safeguards.
There is no bucket policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so objects may be retrieved over unencrypted HTTP.

A file named customer-master.xlsx is uploaded with no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument into aws_s3_bucket.data, which is unencrypted and potentially public, exposing sensitive customer records.
The financials bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial data is stored without enforced encryption at rest.
Although the ACL is private, no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated, so a later ACL or bucket policy change could silently make financial data publicly accessible.
No logging block is configured, leaving access to financial data unaudited.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy = true is set, so financial objects can be permanently overwritten or destroyed with no recovery path.
No bucket policy enforces aws:SecureTransport, permitting cleartext HTTP access to financial data in transit.

The operations bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 default encryption. Any data written to this bucket is unprotected at rest by customer-controlled keys.

The operations bucket defines no logging block, so access to objects is not recorded to the logs bucket. Absence of an audit trail hinders detection and forensic investigation of unauthorised data access.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a later ACL or bucket policy change could expose its contents publicly. The private ACL alone is not a defence-in-depth control.
The data_science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving potentially sensitive analytics datasets stored unencrypted by default.
No public access block is configured for this bucket, so account- or bucket-level public access protections are not enforced and a future policy/ACL change could expose the data.
The centralised log bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so nothing prevents a bucket policy or ACL from making audit logs publicly readable.
The log destination bucket itself has no logging configuration, so tampering with or reading of stored audit logs is not itself audited.
None of the buckets in this excerpt enforce aws:SecureTransport via a bucket policy, so requests may be served over unencrypted HTTP, allowing log and dataset contents to be read in transit.
